title: Find the first match and look at nothing after it

blocks.text: Intermediate operations are **lazy**: nothing runs until a terminal operation asks for elements, and a **short-circuiting** terminal operation such as `findFirst()` stops asking as soon as it has its answer.

Write `FirstMatch.firstMatch(List<String> names, Predicate<String> test, List<String> examined)`. It returns the first name that `test` accepts, as an `Optional<String>`. Every name your pipeline actually hands to `test` must also be appended to `examined`, in the order it was examined, after whatever the list already holds, so the caller can see how far the stream went.
A pipeline that gathers every match before choosing one gives the right name but examines too much; and "no match" is an answer too.

cases.says: It returns the first name the test accepts.
Names after the first match are never examined: findFirst short-circuits a lazy pipeline.
When no name matches, every name is examined and the answer is an empty Optional, not an exception.

concepts: An empty stream is handled gracefully: findFirst answers it with an empty Optional.
Intermediate operations are lazy, so a short-circuiting terminal operation such as findFirst stops at the first match.
